## How I learn best  (CONFIRMED PATTERNS — gated, see update rules)
<!-- Empty by design. Patterns land here ONLY after the tutor proposes one and you
     explicitly agree — usually during a lesson wrap-up. Until then the tutor teaches
     from the contract's universal defaults. Example of what will accumulate here:
       "Lead with a worked example. Abstractions land only after I've seen one
       concrete case fully worked. (Agreed Lesson 3.)"
-->
- Lead with motivation. I want the *why* up front — a concrete example or a reason this
  matters — before the abstraction. (Confirmed Lesson 1.)
- Weave in brief history. Short historical context — who, when, and why it mattered — lands
  well and is actively valued; keep these brief, in-stride asides rather than detours.
  (Confirmed Lesson 1.)

## Lesson preferences
- Light default structure: a bit of explanation, then dialogue / questions / practice.
  Vary the form by topic — partly to discover what works.
- Freeform and adaptive over scripted. Let interest, mood, and pace steer what
  comes next.
- Surface sources. When drawing on existing explanations, textbooks, or videos, name
  them.
- Stopping: the system can suggest a natural stopping point; I can call it anytime.
  Always give a brief recap at the end.
- Session size is an explicit parameter (tight / standard / deep), set at lesson start.

## Working notes  (tentative — freely updatable)
<!-- The tutor's hunches about how you learn, under test. "Preference guess:" bullets
     accumulate evidence across lessons; strong ones get proposed for promotion into

- The learner is a CS education researcher and educator — STS lessons click when grounded in
  examples from education and technology already familiar from practice.
- The learner reads for argument and message, not just aesthetics — art lessons should
  foreground what movements were saying and why, not just visual style.
- Preference guess: check-questions that reach one step past what's been said land well, even
  when not tired — worth leaning into for practice-question calibration.

## Update rules
- **Working notes**, **Broader prerequisites**, and **Settled questions** — the tutor
  updates freely, any session, without asking.
- **Confirmed patterns** ("How I learn best") — any change (promote in, edit, or
  remove) requires my agreement first. The tutor proposes, I dispose. Mechanically:
  the session patch's `proposedConfirmedPatterns` is surfaced but never applied; only
  `approvedConfirmedPatterns` (after my explicit yes) is written.
- **Interest lanes & distribution** — my deliberate setting; adjust via course-setup
  or honor a per-session override, but don't quietly rewrite it.
